newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FLAT, C.BANK SEEN BUYING DOLLARS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FLAT, C.BANK SEEN BUYING DOLLARS.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 349-354 per dollar, little changed from 348-353 in the morning after foreign currency supply rose and the central bank bought dollars in a thin interbank trade, dealers said.
"Foreign currency supply and demand were balanced amid low market activity and the lev traded sideways near 350," a commercial bank dealer said.
The central bank (BNB) was the main dollar buyer in the market today, buying the currency at 350-351 levs, traders said. Central bank officials declined comment.

Foreign currency supply kept rising on profit taking both on the interbank and the cash market on an anticipated lev rise after the central bank said last week it would act to counter further falls in the lev, traders said.
The lev traded at 335-337 per dollar on the cash market today, up from 340-342 on Tuesday.

The lev has steadied near 350 per dollar since Monday after the BNB said on Friday it had agreed coordinated action with commercial banks to prevent further sharp falls in the lev, which slumped from 275 to 395 last week on a dollar rush.
Many financial houses have been denied byuing foreign currency from banks since Monday as a result.

Local media on Wednesday quoted Prime Minister Zhan Videnov as saying that both the government and the central bank would tighten control on financial houses and exchange bureaus to prevent unlawful speculation against the lev. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
